name: liquid-glass-music-card

frames.best_why: The disc has visibly turned, the progress bar is part-filled, and no cursor covers the controls.

tagline: A spinning vinyl record sits beside the track title, seek bar and controls.
summary: A compact now-playing card with a spinning vinyl disc you can grab to scrub, a progress bar, rolling timestamps and previous, play and next buttons, optionally set on a frosted glass panel.
appearance: A small rounded panel, mildly transparent, holding a black vinyl disc with a bright printed centre label beside a five-bar level meter and the words Now Playing above a track title and artist. A thin orange progress bar and three round playback buttons sit below.
behaviour: The record turns steadily at 33⅓ speed while the track plays; grabbing the disc and flicking it scrubs the song, and the timestamps roll over digit by digit. Play and pause spin the disc up or down, and next swaps in a new track.
demo_content: Track Low Tide by Pale Harbor, then Static Bloom by Juniper Wire, over a mountain and cloud photo.
use_when: A page needs a self-contained music widget with a tactile disc and standard playback controls.
avoid_when: The glass refraction only renders in Chromium, and the card is capped at max-w-sm so it will not stretch wide.
customise: Tracks array, starting track, autoplay, one accent colour, glass effect and class name are props. The artwork variants and timing constants are fixed in the source.
weight_why: One card with a compositor-driven disc spin and a small meter loop; no canvas or WebGL.

a11y.note: Buttons and the seek slider have labels and keyboard control, but the vinyl disc itself only scrubs by pointer.

issues: The glass filter uses a Chromium-only backdrop URL, so other browsers get a plain tinted panel.
polish_why: Polished playback card with believable record spin; the glass is subtle and the busy photo competes.
